candidates.review: Reads as a quail from the side: plump teardrop body, small head, a forward-curling plume over the bill, smooth sculpt (no feather shards), one main piece with three stray single triangles. Faults: the plume is a thin curled wire plus a few crown spikes, not a teardrop; the crown is pinched into a ridge from the front; the stance is upright and tall (height about equal to length) on legs too long and thin for a quail (about a fifth of the height is bare tarsus); the tail is two long thin blades instead of a short rounded tail; the bill is slim and pointed rather than short and stout; eyes are shallow sockets. Feet: three forward toes and a hind toe, flat. A build script would delete the generated plume and add the procedural teardrop (brief section 6), cut the legs at mid-tarsus and add short grey procedural legs, trim the tail blades to a short fan, and give the body the forage pitch. No species drift to a crestless partridge; scaling and face pattern are colour only.

accuracy_notes: Adopted 2026-10-25 from the Meshy preview. Reads as a California quail at 3-10 m: black face bordered white, chestnut crown, forward topknot, blue-grey breast, brown back, scaled buff belly; female variant (grey-brown head and breast, no face pattern) drawn for half the birds. Still open: the body is the generator's deep teardrop, so even pitched 12 degrees it sits upright and heavy; the short legs (3 cm) are mostly hidden by the grass layer; the belly scaling and flank streaks are a face-sized mottle, not a pattern; the face border is blocky at lod0 and gone at lod1; the female plume keeps the male's size. A local birder should check the plume shape, leg length and posture.
